game: LA @ SF, 2025-11-09 16:25 ET, outdoor, SF +5.5, total 49.5

script.base: Market has LA leading a moderate game (implied LA 27.5, SF 22.0 on a 49.5 total), not a slog and not a shootout. LA is ahead by about a score late, Stafford has already been living on Davante Adams (24 targets, 134 yards, 296 air in weeks 6/7/9), and the close-out carries go to Kyren Williams (50 carries, 218 yards in that window) with Blake Corum mixed in (30/118). SF, as a +5.5 dog, throws to stay in range: Christian McCaffrey (20 targets) and Jauan Jennings (19 targets, 210 air) plus George Kittle (11), not a buried Jake Tonges.
script.flip1: Brock Purdy (toe, Questionable) sits or is capped and the SF dropback game shrinks. M.Jones is the only other SF name with a real L3 rush line (8/41), so a backup-QB game would lean checkdown/CMC and designed runs; Jennings' downfield air yards die and LA's run script gets fatter.
script.flip2: SF hangs around or leads. LA cannot salt the clock, Corum's change-up carries vanish behind Kyren on passing downs, and Stafford's air yards (Adams 296, Ferguson 141) spike. The other blowout path, LA up big, risks starter receiving snaps late but feeds LA RB rush overs.

Jake Tonges is not on the report, and neither is Kittle, so both are available with Kittle holding the recent TE targets.

Jennings (210 air) is the SF piece that can attack explosives/left, but he is the second option and Purdy is Questionable.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost. Corum: SF jumped ahead, the game never became a clock-kill, and McVay kept Kyren (50 L3 carries, and the passing-down back) on the field, so Corum's 37 and 58 were leftover from a different script and he finished around the 13-yard game that opened his last4. Or the whole SF front-seven question cluster played and 4.29 YPC tightened back under 3.5. Tonges: the 2-yard game was a one-week snap quirk, Kittle left early with something not on this report, and Tonges inherited the 11-target TE role and cleared 31.5 on two crossers — Bartch sitting would have pushed SF into that quick game. That Tonges counter is narrower than Corum's, because Kittle is not on the injury report and three straight listed games already exclude Tonges from the target tree. The Corum counter is real but not stronger than the carry trend plus the Williams-out front, so it stays a lean instead of a drop. Weather was not saved; a 15 mph wind would have helped the Corum over and not hurt the Tonges under.
slip_story: One story, not a bet: LA is the 27.5 side and closes on the ground, so the back who already owns a rising third of the carries clears a low rushing median, while SF's throws — chase-mode or not — stay with McCaffrey, Jennings and Kittle, so Tonges' stale 31.5 median misses. Those two do not need opposite scripts. Do not add a total under, do not add Kyren rush over on the same carries, and do not add Jennings over until Purdy is confirmed active.
